На телефоне теперь **диагностическая сборка** — это ещё не починка, а замер. Внизу слева на 3D-вьюпорте появилась панелька.

Что прошу сделать (полминуты):

1. Подключитесь к роботу, откройте **Live**, дождитесь модели. Панелька должна показывать `container: in scene`, `camera: in scene`, `make ran: 1x`.
2. Переключитесь на **Camera**, потом обратно на **3D** — тот самый первый возврат, где модели нет.
3. Посмотрите на панельку и скажите, что в ней: `container` — `in scene` или `DETACHED`? Сколько `children`? Что в `phase` и `make ran`?
4. Нажмите кнопку **re-append**. Модель появилась?

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
Каждая строчка панельки отсекает свою ветку, поэтому ответ будет однозначным, а не «похоже на»:

- **`DETACHED`** — сущности вынесло из сцены. Тогда виноват отложенный teardown старой сцены, и чинить надо повторной вставкой при появлении, а не отвязкой перед вставкой (что я и сделал в прошлый раз мимо цели).
- **`in scene`, но пусто** — сущности на месте, значит проблема в рендере: свет или камера. Тогда `children` покажет, цело ли дерево.
- **`children: 1`** вместо двух (свет + модель робота) — дерево разобрали, причина глубже, в `RobotSceneGraph`.
- **`make ran: 1x`** после возврата — вьюха вообще не пересоздавалась, и тогда неверна вся моя модель происходящего.

Кнопка `re-append` — прямая проверка фикса: если картинка возвращается по нажатию, то починка это то же самое, но автоматически.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

- Цветовой коммит `b5d15d5` эту диагностику **не содержит** — она поверх, и я её сниму, как только причина будет ясна.

- Going off screen calls `pauseStream()`, not `stop()`: `stop()` clears `geometryTask` and `start()` guards on it
  being nil, so the pair re-downloads the URDF and re-frames the camera.
- **The camera entity is the one thing that must _not_ survive a `RealityView` teardown.** Everything else is
  deliberately reused across the 3D/camera switch — the meshes, the entity tree, the lighting, the angle. But
  "the camera we render from" is a role the _scene_ holds, not a property the entity carries: append the same
  `PerspectiveCamera` to the replacement scene and it is present without being active, so nothing at all is drawn.
  `OrbitCamera.makeEntity()` builds a new one per view and applies the stored angle to it; the controller then
  writes to that instance. The failure is silent and looks like an empty viewport with `phase == .ready`,
  `container.scene` non-nil and the full child count — no property of the entity graph reveals it, because the
  entity graph is fine. Reproducing it needs the real screen: a bare box in a two-branch `ViewBuilder` swap does
  _not_ show it, since a trivial view tree releases the old scene before the new one is made.

# ReachyScene

RealityKit rendering of the robot, driven by the state stream. Depends on ReachyKit. Read-only — nothing here
ever sends the robot a command.

- An `Entity` has one parent, so there must be **exactly one live `RealityView` per `RobotSceneModel`** — a second
  one silently steals the robot from the first. Move the view; never mount two (this rules out zoom transitions and
  `if/else` layout branches, both of which keep source and destination alive at once).
- Going off screen calls `pauseStream()`, not `stop()`: `stop()` clears `geometryTask` and `start()` guards on it
  being nil, so the pair re-downloads the URDF and re-frames the camera.

lines: `if/else` layout branches, both of which keep source and destination alive at once).
- Going off screen calls `pauseStream()`, not `stop()`: `stop()` clears `geometryTask` and `start()` guards on it
being nil, so the pair re-downloads the URDF and re-frames the camera.
+- **The camera entity is the one thing that must _not_ survive a `RealityView` teardown.** Everything else is
+  deliberately reused across the 3D/camera switch — the meshes, the entity tree, the lighting, the angle. But
+  "the camera we render from" is a role the _scene_ holds, not a property the entity carries: append the same
+  `PerspectiveCamera` to the replacement scene and it is present without being active, so nothing at all is drawn.
+  `OrbitCamera.makeEntity()` builds a new one per view and applies the stored angle to it; the controller then
+  writes to that instance. The failure is silent and looks like an empty viewport with `phase == .ready`,

+  _not_ show it, since a trivial view tree releases the old scene before the new one is made.

git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
fix(scene): rebuild the camera per RealityView so 3D returns on the first switch

Switching the viewport to the camera and back left the 3D view empty. Doing it a
second time brought the robot back, which read as a race and was not one.

Everything about the scene deliberately survives the swap — the downloaded meshes,
the entity tree, the lighting rig, the angle the user dragged to — because
re-downloading a URDF to change tabs is not acceptable. One `PerspectiveCamera` was
being carried across with them, and that is the single thing that cannot be: which
camera a scene renders from is a role the *scene* holds, not a property the entity
carries. Appended to the replacement scene it is present without being active, and
a scene with no active camera draws nothing at all.

Which is exactly what made this hard to see. On the empty screen `phase` is `ready`,
`container.scene` is non-nil and points at the current scene, the child count is
right, and the camera entity is in that scene too. No property of the entity graph
is wrong, because the entity graph is not what is wrong. Two fixes aimed at it —
`removeFromParent()` before appending, then reparenting under a fresh root — changed
nothing, and a bare box in a two-branch `ViewBuilder` swap does not reproduce it at
all: a trivial view tree releases the old scene before the new one is made, so the
role is reassigned. It took an on-screen probe on real hardware to get the fact that
mattered, which was `make ran: 2x` next to a scene id that had not gone stale.

`OrbitCamera` now vends a camera per view and keeps writing to the newest one, so
the viewpoint carries over without the entity doing so. Covered by two tests, since
the rendering itself is not testable here.
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -6

Готово. Дерево чистое, два коммита.

**`078ecd9`** — цвет. Снят `.darkTitleBar()`, убраны подложки у 3D-вьюпорта и у камеры, вместе с ними ушёл прибитый белый у «Connecting…». Плюс сид выбора вкладки и превью `Root — live tab`, которого не было, и 11 перезаписанных референсов.

**`579f70c`** — камера. `OrbitCamera` выдаёт новую сущность на каждую вьюху и продолжает писать в актуальную, так что угол обзора переезжает без переезда самой камеры. Два теста.

Проверено: 545 тестов, 187 снапшотов, SwiftLint `--strict` на 792 файлах — всё зелёное. sim-daemon и симулятор погашены.

Две вещи, где я ошибся по ходу, чтобы это не осталось в тумане:

**Я сказал «закоммичено», не посмотрев состав.** В `b5d15d5` попали только PNG и `Package.resolved` — ни одного исходника. Я прочитал «20 files changed» и счёл это подтверждением. Ветка не выложена, так что дополнил коммит недостающим (`078ecd9`), но заявление было неверным в момент, когда я его сделал. Попутно выяснилось, что записанное в CLAUDE.md правило 6 — «хук стейджит каждый изменённый `.swift` и `.md`» — работает не так: до-стейджит он только то, что сам переформатировал. Стоит поправить в документации отдельно.

**Три гипотезы подряд оказались неверны**, и все три я проверял правками, а не замерами: протухший родитель → `removeFromParent()`, отложенный teardown → перепривязка, и уже потом камера. Первые две стоили двух сборок на вашем устройстве.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
Что тут сработало и стоит запомнить: **диагностика на экране вместо логов**. Панелька с `make ran`, идентификаторами сцен и состоянием родителя дала за два круга то, чего рассуждения не дали за три попытки — и решающей строкой оказалась `make ran: 2x` рядом с несменившимся id сцены. Именно эта пара исключила разом и «вьюха не пересоздалась», и «сущности в старой сцене».

Второе — **изолированный стенд, который не воспроизвёл баг, оказался ценнее того, который бы воспроизвёл.** Куб в такой же схеме работал исправно, и это сузило поиск до того, чем сцена робота отличается от куба. Отрицательный результат отсёк целый класс объяснений.

Третье, уже про сам предмет: у большинства сущностей есть только геометрия, и она переезжает вместе с объектом. У камеры есть ещё и роль, а роль принадлежит сцене. Ни `container.scene`, ни `children`, ни `parent` на этот вопрос не отвечают — потому замер и показывал «всё в порядке» при пустом экране. Записал в `Sources/ReachyScene/AGENTS.md` вместе с приметой отказа и с тем фактом, что тривиальный стенд его не ловит.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

На телефоне сейчас последняя сборка — уже без диагностической панельки, с обоими фиксами.

I'm reviewing what I've learned from this session and noticing a critical error in the documentation. Rule 6 in CLAUDE.md claims the pre-commit hook stages every modified Swift and Markdown file, but that's not what actually happens—it only re-stages the files it actually reformatted. My recent commit shows this clearly: it contained only PNGs and Package.resolved changes even though seven Swift and Markdown files had been modified.

I should verify this against the hk.pkl configuration to confirm what the `stage` command actually does, since this is a material correction that affected my commit history.

There's also a timing issue I discovered with the device build loop—`devicectl device process launch` sometimes doesn't report "Launched" immediately after an install, especially when chained together. Adding a sleep between them resolved it, though this feels more like a device-specific gotcha than something critical for the main documentation.

The snapshot capture for the root-connected iPhone is essentially blank, which appears to be a pre-existing limitation rather than something I introduced. The sim-daemon setup in a fresh worktree takes over 14 minutes because of pip installs, and since `.venv-sim` is created per-worktree, each new one pays that full cost again. I also caught that my poll script was returning exit code 0 on timeout—that was my mistake, not the project's. For Prefire/Tuist, deleting a file from the Apps directories requires running `mise run project` to regenerate, just like adding files do, so that's worth noting alongside the existing documentation.

One thing that caught me: putting a preview harness in `Apps/ReachySpike/Previews/` didn't compile it into the target—it only feeds into the storybook playbook. I had to move it to `Sources/` for it to actually build, which cost a cycle to discover. That's a gotcha worth documenting.

Now I'm prioritizing what goes into CLAUDE.md. The highest-impact items are the ones most likely to trip people up again: the hook staging rule correction, the fact that `Apps/*/Previews/` files don't compile into the app target, that deleting a file requires `mise run project`, the per-worktree `.venv-sim` environment quirk, and the compact root snapshot issue. I should verify the hook staging claim and the environment setup behavior before adding them.

Предлагаю пять правок, все в корневой [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md).

### 1. Правило 6 — сейчас оно неверно и сегодня из-за него ушёл неполный коммит

**Почему:** документ обещает, что хук сам застейджит все изменённые `.swift`/`.md`. На деле `hk run pre-commit` работает по индексу и до-стейджит только собственные исправления — семь изменённых файлов в коммит не попали, а я отчитался об успехе по числу файлов.

```diff
-6. **Conventional commits** — enforced by the commit-msg hook. The pre-commit hook stages _every_ modified `*.swift`
-   and `*.md` (`stage` in `hk.pkl`), not only what you `git add` — separate unrelated edits with
-   `git stash push <paths>` first, or they land in one commit. Only those two extensions: `.py`, `.json`, fixtures
-   and hook scripts need an explicit `git add`, and a commit with nothing staged fails before the hook runs.
+6. **Conventional commits** — enforced by the commit-msg hook. `stage` in `hk.pkl` re-stages what the hooks
+   _reformatted_, nothing more: `hk run pre-commit` works off the index, so a modified file you did not `git add`
+   stays out of the commit whatever its extension. `git add` everything you mean to ship and check the result with
+   `git show --stat` — a commit that silently carried only its PNGs read as "20 files changed" and looked fine.
+   A commit with nothing staged fails before the hook runs.
```

### 2. Слепое пятно снапшотов

**Почему:** `Root-connected`, `Root-no-camera` и `Root-unreachable` на iPhone — один и тот же файл. Правки в компактной раскладке проходят «зелёными» без всякой проверки.

```diff
+`Root-connected`, `Root-no-camera` and `Root-unreachable` are **byte-identical on iPhone** — the compact connected
+root captures as a near-blank ghost, so those three references distinguish nothing and a change to that layout
+passes untested. The iPad captures of the same previews are the ones carrying the layout.
```

### 3. `Apps/*/Previews/**` не компилируется в само приложение

**Почему:** стоило цикла сборки — файл там невидим для `ReachySpike` (`cannot find … in scope`).

```diff
+`Apps/<App>/Previews/**` is in the storybook and snapshot targets' `sources`, **not** in the app target's
+(`ReachySpike/Sources/**` only) — a helper the app itself must see goes in `Sources/`.
```

### 4. Удаление файла тоже требует регенерации

**Почему:** в CLAUDE.md описано только добавление; удаление даёт `Build input file cannot be found`, что читается как поломка проекта.

```diff
-  Prefire reads previews off the filesystem; Xcode compiles the file list Tuist baked in.
+  Prefire reads previews off the filesystem; Xcode compiles the file list Tuist baked in — **deleting** a file
+  needs `mise run project` just as much as adding one, or the build fails with `Build input file cannot be found`.
```

### 5. Стоимость первого `sim-daemon` в новом worktree

**Почему:** я дважды счёл его сломанным, а он просто ставил зависимости; `.venv-sim` не переиспользуется между worktree.

```diff
+`.venv-sim` is per-worktree and gitignored, so the first `sim-daemon` in a fresh one spends 10–15 minutes in pip
+(mujoco, GStreamer) before binding :8000 — it is installing, not hung. Watch `.venv-sim` growing, not the port.
```

file.content:
[tasks.sim-daemon]
description = "Run simulated Reachy Mini daemon (MuJoCo) reachable from LAN devices"
run = """
#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail
# macOS: MuJoCo GUI requires mjpython, and uv has known MuJoCo issues — plain pip venv.
VENV=.venv-sim
REQUIREMENTS=Scripts/sim-requirements.txt
STAMP="$VENV/.requirements.sha256"
EXPECTED="$(shasum -a 256 "$REQUIREMENTS" | awk '{print $1}')"
# Explicit path: system PATH can shadow mise's python with an ancient one.
PYTHON="$(./bin/mise where python)/bin/python3"
INSTALLED="$(test -f "$STAMP" && cat "$STAMP" || true)"
if [ ! -x "$VENV/bin/mjpython" ] || [ "$INSTALLED" != "$EXPECTED" ]; then
  rm -rf "$VENV"
  "$PYTHON" -m venv "$VENV"
  "$VENV/bin/python" -m pip install --quiet --requirement "$REQUIREMENTS"
  printf '%s' "$EXPECTED" > "$STAMP"
fi
"$VENV/bin/python" -c 'import importlib.metadata as m; assert m.version("reachy-mini") == "1.9.0"'
# `gstreamer_python`'s libgstpython.dylib segfaults while GStreamer scans plugins.
# Forked (the default) that only surfaces as "External plugin loader failed" and
# the daemon then hangs before binding :8000; with GST_REGISTRY_FORK=no the
# segfault kills the daemon outright. The pipeline below needs native elements
# only, so the plugin is pure liability.
find "$VENV" -name libgstpython.dylib -exec mv {} {}.disabled ';' 2>/dev/null || true
# Without the scanner GStreamer's plugin loader silently fails, webrtcsink can't
# find the Opus encoder ("No caps found for stream audio_0") and no WebRTC
# producer is ever registered on :8443.
export GST_PLUGIN_SCANNER="$PWD/$VENV/lib/python3.12/site-packages/gstreamer_libs/libexec/gstreamer-1.0/gst-plugin-scanner"
exec "$VENV/bin/mjpython" -m reachy_mini.daemon.app.main --sim --fastapi-host 0.0.0.0 "$@"
"""

OLD="$(pwd)/.venv-sim"

toolUseResult.originalFile:
# ReachyUI

Shared SwiftUI views for all platforms (macOS/iPadOS/iOS). Depends on ReachyKit and ReachyMedia (WebRTC camera).

- Adaptive layouts, not per-platform copies; `#if os(iOS)` only for platform-exclusive APIs (Settings deep link etc.).
- `horizontalSizeClass` is unavailable on macOS — guard size-class branching with `#if os(macOS)` (always regular there).
- All robot interaction goes through `RobotSession` / `RobotBrowser` from ReachyKit — no direct URLSession here.
- Screen logic belongs in a `@MainActor @Observable` model beside the view (`MovesModel`, `LogConsoleModel`), covered
  by `Tests/ReachyUITests`; the view stays thin. `@Observable` does honour `didSet`, so derived caches can live there.
- `Section` has no title-plus-footer overload: `Section("X") { … } footer: { … }` fails to compile with a misleading
  "generic parameter 'Content' could not be inferred". Either `Section("X") { … }` or the full
  `Section { … } header: { Text("X") } footer: { … }`.
- A container view taking a closure argument _and_ two trailing `@ViewBuilder`s trips SwiftLint's
  `multiple_closures_with_trailing_closure`. Pass the extra behaviour as a child view instead
  (`OnboardingBackButton`), not as a third closure.
- `background(_:)` defaults to `ignoresSafeAreaEdges: .all`, so a full-bleed backdrop also paints the inset the
  floating tab bar sits in — bottom on iPhone, top on iPad. That bar is glass and renders whatever it finds there, so
  it turns dark on that one tab, a frame behind the switch. Neither viewport paints a backdrop any more: the 3D scene
  and the camera's letterbox both take the system background, so the chrome over them stays legible in both
  appearances. **Do not pin a colour under adaptive chrome** — every such backdrop drags a pinned foreground along
  with it, and then neither half can be removed alone. The Live tab's `Color.black` forced
  `toolbarColorScheme(.dark)` to keep the title readable (drop one and the title goes white-on-white or
  black-on-black); the camera's forced a white `Connecting…` for the same reason. `RTCMTLVideoView` clears its own
  unfilled area, so the video never needed the SwiftUI backdrop — that one only ever painted the safe-area insets.
- Deployment floor is iOS 18 / macOS 15 (`Package.swift`, `Apps/Project.swift`), set by `RealityView`.
  `ScrollPosition`, `onScrollPhaseChange` and `onScrollGeometryChange` are available; the zero-height sentinel row in
  `LogConsoleScreen` predates the bump and is not a required pattern.

## Previews and snapshots

`Previews/` sits here but is **excluded from the SwiftPM target** (`Package.swift`) and compiled only by the Xcode
targets in `Apps/`. `#Preview` is an external macro implemented by `libPreviewsMacros.dylib`, which ships inside
Xcode's platform SDKs and not in the pinned swift.org toolchain — a `#Preview` anywhere under a SwiftPM target breaks
`mise run build`, `mise run test` and CI with "plugin for module 'PreviewsMacros' not found".

Adding a screen (project rule 8) means: a preview per state in `Previews/<Screen>Previews.swift`, whatever seam and
`#if DEBUG` factory those states need, `mise run test:snapshots:record`, and `git add` on the PNGs.

- Preview files use `@testable import ReachyUI`; that is why `ENABLE_TESTABILITY` is set for the whole Xcode project.
- **Prefire reads previews off the filesystem; Xcode compiles the file list Tuist baked in.** A new file under
  `Previews/` is therefore picked up by the generator but not compiled until `mise run project` runs again — which is
  why the snapshot tasks depend on it. A bare `xcodebuild` skips that and fails with "cannot find … in scope".
- Anything a preview body references must be visible target-wide, because Prefire copies the body into a separate
  generated file. Shared wrappers live in `PreviewScene`; a `private` helper compiles locally and breaks the test.
- **A preview with no `traits:` is captured at full device size.** Prefire defaults the trait list to `.device`
  (`RawPreviewModel.isScreen`), and that device trait is what carries `horizontalSizeClass` — so it is what makes the
  iPad snapshot exercise the regular-width layout. Components opt out with `traits: .sizeThatFitsLayout`.
- **A preview must be final on its first frame.** Prefire captures synchronously and its `.snapshot(delay:)` modifier
  lives in a module this target cannot import without breaking the macOS build. Never rely on a `.task` completing —
  hand the view a model that is already in its end state (`AudioSettingsModel.preview()`, `RobotSession.preview()`).
- Model preview factories live **in the model's own file** under `#if DEBUG`, not in `Previews/`: they write members
  that are `private` to that file, and `@testable` does not reach `private`.
- Screens take their model through an initialiser with a default (`init(session:model:)`), so production call sites
  are unchanged and previews inject a frozen one.
- A defaulted argument whose value is `@MainActor` (`= SpikeModel()`, `= .preview()`) compiles in the SwiftPM targets
  but not in the `Apps/` ones, where it is evaluated nonisolated. Use `nil` and resolve it in the body.
- A model that already takes a factory closure (`OnboardingModel(session:)`, `BLEConsoleModel(link:)`) needs no new
  seam — hand it a `BLELink.preview(…)`, which sits on an inert `PreviewBLETransport` and is assigned its state
  directly. Building the link is not enough on its own: `OnboardingModel.session` is only set by `beginScan()`, which
  is the CoreBluetooth call a preview must not make, so the factory assigns it.
- A screen whose `.task` guards on `model == nil` needs no `reachyPreviewMode` check — injecting the model is what
  makes it inert. Add the guard only where the effect runs unconditionally (`WiFiSettingsCard`, `LogConsoleScreen`).
- Not covered, deliberately: `SceneViewport` in `.ready` (a bare `RealityView`) and `CameraViewport` in `.streaming`
  (Metal-backed `RTCMTLVideoView`). Neither renders anything meaningful headless — snapshot their overlay phases.
- One `RobotSceneModel` per preview: `ReachyScene/AGENTS.md` requires exactly one live `RealityView` per model.
- **Navigation chrome does not stay inside a preview card.** SwiftUI hoists `.toolbar` and
  `.searchable` out of the storybook's scaled cards into the app's own bars, even though each
  preview brings its own `NavigationStack` — this is the limitation Prefire records as
  "NavigationView in Preview not supported for Playbook". The storybook hides its root bars to
  absorb it; `LogConsoleScreen`'s search field still floats over the catalogue, which is cosmetic
  and not worth contorting the screen for. Snapshots are unaffected — they capture the title _and_
  the toolbar items, so `RobotScreen`'s Settings gear and `MovesScreen`'s Refresh are covered.
  Only the storybook hoists.

Actually, I think the real issue is the GStreamer registry cache. GStreamer writes a registry file to `~/.cache/gstreamer-1.0/registry.*.bin`, and if that registry was built while scanning the cache venv's plugins and something failed, it could be poisoned with stale entries pointing to the old relocated venv path that I deleted. Even though I reinstalled at the same path, the registry might still be holding references that break the plugin loader. The most likely culprit is actually a macOS Gatekeeper or code signing issue with the `gst-plugin-scanner` binary itself. The scanner is a helper binary that GStreamer forks, and while I verified it's executable with `test -x`, that only checks the permission bit — macOS might still block execution due to quarantine flags or code signing. role the *scene* holds, not a property the entity carries: appended to the
replacement scene it is present without being active, and a scene with no active
camera draws nothing. `OrbitCamera` now vends one per view and keeps writing to the
newest, so the viewpoint carries over without the entity doing so.

The Live tab had no snapshot at all — every root preview sat on the Robot tab and
`tab` was private state with no seam — which is why the title bug shipped. It takes
a seed now, and `Root — live tab` captures it.

Also recorded in AGENTS.md: three root references are byte-identical on iPhone and
verify nothing; `Apps/<App>/Previews/**` is not in the app target's sources;
deleting a generated-target file needs `mise run project`; `.venv-sim` is
per-worktree and sharing it is a dead end.
EOF
